twistermill.ponder.windroto_ponder.title: Twistermill Bearing
twistermill.ponder.windroto_ponder.heade: Generate rotational power with the Twistermill Bearing
twistermill.ponder.windroto_ponder.text_:
Twistermill bearings convert wind power into dynamic rotation. 
Depending on wind strength, the capacity (SU) fluctuates as well. 

Create machines can be powered with it.
The rotation direction can be set via the movement mode.
The larger wind turbines are built, the more energy they can produce.

When blocks are placed on the top, they become physics objects (Sable sublevel ship). 
Blocks can still be placed afterward, which makes it possible to build Ship-on-Ship objects.

A single block on the top can be expanded into a Ship without glue. With glue, multiple blocks on the top can be transformed into the Ship.
When there is no wind, overstress can occur. A clutch can disengage at low RPM and re-engage when enough wind is available.

Redstone Comparator: 
The signal strength depends on RPM. 
If the wind turbine rotates too slowly, the signal drops to strength 0.
Create Analog Lever or Redstone Link input signals 1-14 activate the brake, while strength 15 brings the wind turbine to a complete stop.
Individual values or summaries can be sent to Create displays.
twistermill.ponder.windvane_ponder.title: Wind Direction Bearing
twistermill.ponder.windvane_ponder.heade: Using the Wind Direction Bearing as a wind vane
twistermill.ponder.windvane_ponder.text_:
A smooth stone slab is required as the north marker (0°). 

Hold a compass in your left hand and a smooth stone slab in your right hand while looking at a Wind Direction Bearing to determine north.

First place a block on the top side, then assemble-toggle the bearing (right-click). 

After that, activate Park Mode with a Redstone pulse (stone button). 

Build the Ship Contraption and assemble-toggle every bearing placed from it that represents another Ship anchor. 

Deactivate Park Mode last. This makes bearings on an active Sable Sublevel correctly become new anchor points.

TwisterMill bearings store the last Ship Contraption. 

When disassembled, the bearing includes blocks that were previously part of the Ship Contraption again on the next assemble toggle. 

Newly placed blocks are also recognized as Ship-related.

Added blocks that connect the ground (dirt blocks) to the Ship are ignored. 

Glue is not required in the normal case. 

(does not apply to bearings -> use Park Mode)
When Park Mode is active, the north side (0°) marks the direction the wind comes from once the Ship Contraption has realigned after deactivation.
Park Mode can also be controlled with a Redstone Link.

Display Links are compatible with the Wind Direction Bearing. 

Individual status values or summaries of values can be read and shown on display boards.
twistermill.ponder.adc_plus_servo_ponder: The Control Table is the command center of this ADC setup.
Each ADC Sub System reads one analog redstone value for the Control Table.

The three analog values are normal redstone strengths from 0 to 15.

The paired signal paths carry those values to the three ADC Sub System inputs.

Each ADC Sub System turns one 0-15 signal into a four-bit binary field; together they form the 12-bit command for the Control Table.

The Control Table reads the fields as mode, speed, and angle, and controls launch mode: on change, on pulse, or off.

Open the Control Table with an empty main hand and confirm changes with Accept-SAVE. Without saving, the binary functions will not start.
The Binary Redstone Transmitter outputs the binary code on its top side.

When the Binary Redstone Transmitter sends, the Angle Servo can receive the binary command through its internal Redstone Link.

Set the Angle Servo angle option to 60° RS Link ON, 120° RS Link ON, or 240° RS Link ON.

Insert matching frequency items, then right-click the internal Redstone Link side with a Create Wrench to enable receiving.
With the command received, the Angle Servo top moves the attached contraption through the target angles.

When the servo mode is set to "Mode 3", it becomes a freely rotating bearing. If wind effects on sails are enabled in the config and a contraption is built with sails, it reacts to real world wind and aligns with it. (In development - ON/OFF in config)

twistermill.gui.control_table.info.line_: <Accept-SAVE Button> to save the selection / <Cancel Button> to exit.
The redstone signals: 'Speed', 'Angle' and 'Mode' (0-15) are translated into 12 bits.
Binary Redstone Sender transmits the code to a Redstone Link Sender,
Inv/-Servo decodes the code received via the Redstone Link
-> ON Change = Code is sent after the RS signal has changed.
-> ON Pulse   = Code is sent when the down-side RS pulse is detected.
-> OFF        = Code is not sent. Disabled.
twistermill.ponder.servo_ponder.title: Angle Servo
twistermill.ponder.servo_ponder.text_1:
The Angle Servo has the same functions as the Inverted Angle Servo, but rotates in the opposite direction. 

Servos are used to adjust the pitch of wind turbine blades. 

This helps convert wind kinetic energy into torque more efficiently.
twistermill.ponder.servo_ponder.text_2:
- ANALOG  

When Mode 1, 2 or 3 is selected in the GUI, 
side Redstone inputs are active. 

There is one analog Redstone input each for rotation speed and target angle control.
twistermill.ponder.servo_ponder.text_3:
- DIGITAL 

Activate internal Redstone Link receivers: 

Select GUI Mode 4, 5 or 6. 

A blinking Servo indicates that the receiver has not been linked yet. 

To activate the receiver links, place items into the frequency slots and right-click the link with a Create Wrench. 

A message will confirm: Receiver activated.
twistermill.ponder.servo_ponder.text_4:
Display Links are compatible with Angle Servos. 

Various status values can be read and sent to display boards.
twistermill.ponder.servo_ponder.text_5:
TwisterMill bearings remember the last contraption when disassembled. 

Newly placed blocks can be picked up into the Sublevel again on the next assemble, even without glue. 

Function can be toggled off in config - if off: use glue.
twistermill.ponder.invservo_ponder.title: Inverted Angle Servo
twistermill.ponder.invservo_ponder.text_:
The Inverted Angle Servo has the same functions as the Angle Servo, but rotates in the opposite direction. 

Servos are used to adjust the pitch of wind turbine blades. 

This helps convert wind kinetic energy into torque more efficiently.

- ANALOG  

When Mode 1, 2 or 3 is selected in the GUI, 
side Redstone inputs are active. 

There is one analog Redstone input each for rotation speed and target angle control.

- DIGITAL 

Activate internal Redstone Link receivers: 

Select GUI Mode 4, 5 or 6. 

A blinking Servo indicates that the receiver has not been linked yet. 

To activate the receiver links, place items into the frequency slots and right-click the link with a Create Wrench. 

A message will confirm: Receiver activated.

Display Links are compatible with Angle Servos. 

Various status values can be read and sent to display boards.

TwisterMill bearings remember the last Contraption when disassembled. 

Newly placed blocks can then be picked up into the Sublevel again on the next assemble, even without glue. 

Function can be toggled off in config - if off: use glue.
twistermill.ponder.servo_option_7_ponder:
The Wind Direction Bearing forms the anchor of the Ship-on-Ship Contraption. 

If a Ship was detached from the bearing top or is hanging: 
 -> Look at the bearing and run this command: 

/twistermill reseat now

1.) Wind Direction Bearing 

- Park Mode ON during construction. 
--> (base anchor) 


2.) Twistermill Bearing 

- Redstone signal 15 stops rotation 
--> (rotation anchor)


3.) Mode 7: 120° Offset Blade Anchors - Wind Simulation Force on Sails 
--> (three anchor slots for additional Ships) 


4.) 3x Servo 

- controls energy efficiency through blade pitch angle. 
--> (pitch rotation anchors)

Mode 7: 120° Offset Blade Anchors - Wind Simulation Force on Sails 

Blocks placed on the Servo top are inserted into offset slots. 
Once 3 blocks have been placed, the arrangement of 3 additional anchor points is complete.

Servo controls the blade pitch angle. 
This affects the efficiency of the wind turbine.

For the wind turbine to react to the blade pitch angle, the Twistermill Bearing must be linked to servos. 


Right-click first on the Twistermill Bearing with the Binding Stick, then on the servos to connect. 
Sneak right-click clears the created connections.
